## Details

### `admin_active`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Upgrades the connection to an admin socket and confirms the session.

**Payload:** token?: string — JWT; taken from the `adminToken` cookie if omitted

The mandatory first step for an admin client: until it happens the socket counts as an ordinary listener and all admin events are ignored **silently**. The reply is `admin_confirmed` or `admin_error`. Privileges are re-read from the database rather than taken from the token, so permission changes apply without logging in again. A previous session of the same admin is disconnected automatically — only one connection per account stays alive.

### `admin_add_song`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Adds a track from the library to the queue.

**Payload:**

```js
{
  id: 'day/artist - title.mp3',
  title: 'Title', artist: 'Artist',
  orderType: 'lastinline' | 'donated',
}
```

Requires the `queue_manage` privilege. `donated` places the track ahead of ordinary requests. The result arrives as `admin_success` or `admin_error`, not in a callback. A cooldown applies between additions, and the server also refuses if the same track is already adjacent in the queue or the queue no longer fits before the mode switch.

### `admin_go_live`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Puts an admin on air as a host.

**Payload:** no data (the first argument is ignored)

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{
  ok: true,
  queuePaused: false,
  hosts: [ /* who is on air right now */ ],
  pendingGuests: [ /* the queue of guest requests */ ],
  backgroundMusicMode: 'random' | 'hostChoice',
  selectedBackgroundMusicId: null,
}
{ error: { uk: '…', en: '…' } }
```

Requires the `radio_host` privilege and `RADIO_HOSTS_MODE=true` on the server. The number of on-air slots is capped by `MAX_LIVE_HOST_SLOTS`, and a full room returns an error. Calling it again while already live simply confirms the state. On success the socket joins the hosts room and starts receiving its events.

### `admin_guest_action`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Approves or rejects a guest request.

**Payload:**

```js
{ uid: '…', action: 'accept' | 'reject' }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

Requires `radio_host`. If the slot was taken between request and decision, the guest is refused with `reason: "room_full"`.

### `admin_insert_song_group`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Inserts a predefined group of songs into the queue.

**Payload:**

```js
{ groupId: string }
```

Requires **both** `queue_manage` and `settings_groups`, exactly like `POST /api/admin/song-groups/:groupId/insert`. Groups are configured separately through `/api/admin/song-groups`. Has a longer cooldown than single tracks.

### `admin_leave_live`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Ends the host's broadcast.

**Payload:** no arguments

The slot is freed immediately. Disconnecting has the same effect.

### `admin_remove_song`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Removes a track from the queue by position.

**Payload:** position: number — offset from the current track, as in `search_queue`

Requires `queue_manage`. Has its own cooldown — calling too often returns an error with the number of seconds to wait.

### `admin_skip_song`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Skips the current track.

**Payload:** no arguments

Requires `queue_manage`. In stream mode the server refuses while a jingle is playing or the queue is paused by a host. Shares a cooldown with adding tracks.

### `admin_suggestion_action`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Accepts or rejects a listener's song request.

**Payload:**

```js
{ uid: '…', action: 'add' | 'reject' }
```

Requires `queue_manage`. `add` queues the track as `lastinline`. The listener receives `suggestion_result`. If the request already expired, a "not found" error comes back.

### `get_queue`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

A page of the upcoming queue.

**Payload:**

```js
{ offset?: number = 0, limit?: number = 10 }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{
  items: [{ id, title, artist, orderType }],
  total: 42,   // tracks ahead in total
}
```

The reply arrives in the callback. The current track is not included.

### `guest_check_ban`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

Whether this IP address is banned from the broadcast.

**Payload:** no data

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ banned: boolean }
```

Worth calling before showing the request form, to avoid false hope.

### `guest_connect`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

Connects an approved guest to the broadcast.

**Payload:** no data

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true, role: '…', nickname: '…', expiresAt: 1754899200000 }
```

Only succeeds once a host has approved the session and a slot is free. `expiresAt` is when the session will be cut off; the duration comes from the radio settings. From then on the guest uses the same microphone events as a host.

### `guest_leave_live`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

The guest leaves the broadcast.

**Payload:** no arguments

### `guest_request`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

A listener asks to join the broadcast.

**Payload:**

```js
{ nickname: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true }
{ error: … , secsLeft?: number }
```

The request joins a queue shown to hosts; the decision arrives as `guest_request_result`. Admins cannot submit one. A cooldown and an IP ban check apply.

### `host_audio_chunk`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

A chunk of microphone audio to mix into the broadcast.

**Payload:** Buffer / ArrayBuffer — raw audio data

Accepted only while the microphone is enabled via `host_mic_toggle` — otherwise chunks are silently dropped. This is the hottest channel in the protocol: it streams continuously while the host speaks.

### `host_get_background_music_list`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

A page of available background music.

**Payload:**

```js
{ offset?: number = 0, limit?: number = 5 }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ items: [ … ], total: 12, mode: 'day' }
```

The list depends on the radio's current mode. `limit` is capped at 50. Non-hosts receive an empty list.

### `host_guest_kick`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Removes a guest from the broadcast.

**Payload:**

```js
{ targetId: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

### `host_guest_mute`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Mutes a guest's microphone.

**Payload:**

```js
{ targetId: string, muted: boolean }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

### `host_mic_gain`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Changes your microphone level in the mix.

**Payload:**

```js
{ gain: number }
```

### `host_mic_toggle`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Turns the on-air microphone on or off.

**Payload:**

```js
{ on: boolean }
```

While the microphone is off the server discards audio chunks from this socket. Applies to both hosts and guests.

### `host_pause_queue`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Pauses the track queue — "just chatting" mode.

**Payload:** no arguments

Available to hosts only, not guests. Background music fills the silence, and in every listener's `sync` the `title` becomes `"Just chatting"`.

### `host_resume_queue`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Resumes queue playback.

**Payload:** no arguments

### `host_set_background_music`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Chooses the track that plays while the queue is paused.

**Payload:**

```js
{ trackId: string | null }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

`null` restores random selection. Only meaningful when `backgroundMusicMode` is `hostChoice`.

### `listener_init`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Registers the connection as a listener and asks for an art token.

**Payload:** no arguments

The server does not hand out the token by itself — until the client sends this event, no `listener_uid` arrives and art, lyrics and audio stay closed. Admin connections ignore this event.

### `moderator_ban_ip`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Bans an IP address manually.

**Payload:**

```js
{ ip: string, nickname?: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true, entry: { … } } or { error: … }
```

### `moderator_ban_participant`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Bans a broadcast participant by IP.

**Payload:**

```js
{ targetId: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

Works for guests only: hosts cannot be banned. Requires the SQL provider.

### `moderator_deactivate_guest_code`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Deactivates the current access code.

**Payload:** no data

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true }
```

### `moderator_generate_guest_code`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Creates a special-guest access code.

**Payload:**

```js
{ ttlHours?: number }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true, code: "…", expiresAt: 1754899200000 }
```

If an active code already exists an error is returned — deactivate it first, or use `moderator_regenerate_guest_code`. The code lets someone join the broadcast without queueing, via `special_guest_connect`.

### `moderator_get_banlist`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The list of banned IP addresses.

**Payload:**

```js
{ offset?: number = 0, limit?: number = 10 }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ list: [ … ], total: 7 }
```

Requires `DATA_PROVIDER=sql` — otherwise the list is unavailable.

### `moderator_get_guest_code`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The current special-guest access code.

**Payload:** no data

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ code: "…" } — or { code: null } when no code is active
```

### `moderator_get_live_roster`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Who is on air right now.

**Payload:** no data

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ roster: [ … ], hostsOnline: true }
```

Without the privilege an empty roster is returned, not an error.

### `moderator_kick`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Removes a participant from the broadcast.

**Payload:**

```js
{ targetId: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

The participant receives `host_force_disconnect` or `guest_force_disconnect`.

### `moderator_mute`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Mutes any participant of the broadcast.

**Payload:**

```js
{ targetId: string, muted: boolean }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

Unlike `host_guest_mute`, this also works on hosts.

### `moderator_regenerate_guest_code`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Replaces the current access code with a new one.

**Payload:**

```js
{ ttlHours?: number }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true, code: "…", expiresAt: … }
```

The old code stops working immediately.

### `moderator_unban_ip`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Lifts a ban on an IP address.

**Payload:**

```js
{ ip: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true } or { error: … }
```

### `monitor_answer`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

WebRTC answer for the host's personal monitoring channel.

**Payload:**

```js
{ sdp: … }
```

A private low-latency channel for hearing the broadcast — separate from the shared MP3 stream, which lags. Requires the UDP ports `HOST_MONITOR_ICE_PORT_MIN`–`MAX` to be open.

### `monitor_ice_candidate`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

An ICE candidate for the monitoring channel.

**Payload:** a WebRTC candidate object

### `search_queue`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Searches the upcoming queue.

**Payload:**

```js
{ query?: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
[{ id, title, artist, orderType, position }]
```

`position` is the offset from the current track, and it is exactly what `admin_remove_song` expects. An empty query returns the whole queue.

### `special_guest_connect`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

Joins the broadcast with a one-off code, skipping the queue.

**Payload:**

```js
{ code: string, nickname: string }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true, … } or { error: … }
```

The code is issued by a moderator. Attempts are rate-limited, and an expired or deactivated code returns an error.

### `stream_get_seek`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Asks for the current position of the shared stream (stream mode only).

**Payload:** clientTs: number — the client's local time

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ seek: 87.2, duration: 214.5, trackId: 'day/artist - title.mp3' }
```

Only needed to display a timer: in stream mode the audio itself is synchronous by construction. Outside stream mode the server does not reply at all.

### `stream_ping`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Measures round-trip latency to the server.

**Payload:** clientTs: number

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ serverTs: number, clientTs: number }
```

The server echoes your `clientTs` unchanged — the round-trip difference gives you a latency estimate for more accurate positioning.

### `suggest_song`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Request a song from the library to be played.

**Payload:**

```js
// a song object from GET /api/library
{ id: 'day/artist - title.mp3', title: 'Title', artist: 'Artist' }
```

**Acknowledgement payload:**

```js
{ ok: true }
{ error: 'cooldown', secsLeft: 240 }
{ error: 'no_admin' }   // no online admin with queue rights
{ error: 'no_uid' }     // listener_init was never sent
```

Uses an acknowledgement callback — the second argument to `emit`. The error codes here are **plain strings**, not locale objects, unlike the rest of the API. The cooldown is 5 minutes per `uid`; a request expires after 5 minutes if no admin responds.

### `admin_authorized`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

A helper admin has activated their account with a password of their own.

Until then the account has `authorized: false` and can do nothing.

### `admin_confirmed`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

Session confirmed; carries the current permissions.

**Payload:**

```js
{
  role: 'super_admin' | 'admin',
  privileges: ['queue_manage', '…'],
  authorized: true,   // false = the helper has not activated themselves yet
}
```

Build your interface from this list rather than from the token contents. `authorized: false` means a helper admin still has to set their own password.

### `admin_error`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

An admin action failed.

**Payload:** a JSON string containing a locale object

The payload is a **string**, not an object: `JSON.parse` it first, then pick a language. The same applies to `admin_success`.

### `admin_online`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Whether an admin able to accept requests is online.

**Payload:** boolean

Broadcast to all listeners. `false` means `suggest_song` will fail with `no_admin`, so the request button is worth hiding.

### `admin_success`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

An admin action succeeded.

**Payload:** a JSON string containing a locale object

Often carries a `code` field for machine handling. See `admin_error`.

### `audit_new_entry`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

A new entry in the audit log.

**Payload:** an entry object — the same shape as in `GET /api/admin/audit`

Lets you append to the log live instead of re-fetching the whole list.

### `background_music_now_playing`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Which track is currently filling the pause.

**Payload:**

```js
{ trackId: '…', filename: '…' }   // both null when background music is stopped
```

### `background_music_selection_changed`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

A host picked a different background track.

Keeps the choice in sync between multiple hosts on air.

### `background_music_updated`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The background music library has changed.

A signal to re-read the list via `host_get_background_music_list`.

### `donation_result`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Outcome of a donation order: the song was queued or not.

**Payload:**

```js
{ donationId, accepted: true, tier: 2 | null, song: { title, artist } }
{ donationId, accepted: false, reason: 'payment_failed' | 'no_slot' }
```

Sent only to the socket whose `listener_uid` matches the donor (both are derived from IP). `no_slot` means the payment was confirmed but the song could not be queued (e.g. not enough time before a mode switch) — the donation is marked `paid_unqueued` and stays visible to the admin in the donation history.

### `force_logout`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The session was terminated externally.

**Payload:**

```js
{ reason: 'admin_deleted' }
```

The account was deleted or revoked. The client should clear its state and return the user to the login screen.

### `guest_code_updated`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The special-guest access code has changed.

A signal for other admins to refresh the code they display, so two moderators do not dictate different codes.

### `guest_force_disconnect`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

The guest's participation was ended externally.

Causes: removal, a ban, or the `expiresAt` time limit. The client must stop the microphone and tear down the broadcast UI.

### `guest_pending_status`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

The state of a guest's request while they wait.

### `guest_queue_update`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

The queue of guest requests.

Sent only to admins holding the `radio_host` privilege.

### `guest_request_result`

<Badge type="info" text="guest" />

The decision on a guest's request.

**Payload:**

```js
{ accepted: true, nickname: '…' }
{ accepted: false, auto: false, reason: 'room_full' }
```

`reason: "room_full"` means the slot was taken while the request waited. After `accepted: true` the client must send `guest_connect`.

### `host_force_disconnect`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

The host's broadcast was ended externally.

Arrives on removal by a moderator or a forced session end. The client must tear down the broadcast UI and stop capturing the microphone.

### `host_queue_pause_state`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

The queue has been paused or resumed.

**Payload:**

```js
{ paused: boolean }
```

Hosts room only. Listeners see this state through `sync`.

### `jingles_updated`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The set of jingles has changed.

A signal to re-read the list. Jingles only exist in the cloud + sql + stream configuration.

### `library_updated`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The library changed: a track was added, edited, moved or deleted.

**Payload:** no data — it is only a signal to re-read

Broadcast to **everyone**, not just admins. The signal does not say what changed, so simply re-request the list you need — `/api/admin/songs` for an admin UI or `/api/library` for a listener. Emitted from several places: after an upload, after saving in the editor, after a mode change and after bulk operations.

### `listener_uid`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

The reply to `listener_init`: listener identity and art token.

**Payload:**

```js
{
  uid: '…',                 // derived from the IP; the client does not choose it
  artToken: '…',
  artTokenExpiresIn: 3600,  // seconds
  cooldownSecsLeft: 0,      // until the next song request is allowed
}
```

Listeners behind a shared NAT receive the same `uid`, and therefore share a token and a song-request cooldown.

### `live_hosts_roster`

<Badge type="info" text="host" />

Who is currently on air: hosts and guests.

Sent to the hosts room on every change of line-up. Ordinary listeners never receive it.

### `phrases_updated`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The set of phrases has changed.

A signal to re-read the list. Unlike jingles, there is no `stream_phrase_start`/`stream_phrase_end`: a phrase is mixed into the song rather than replacing it, so listener-facing track metadata never changes.

### `privileges_updated`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

This admin's permissions have just changed.

**Payload:**

```js
{ privileges: ['queue_manage', '…'], authorized: true }
```

Sent to the admin whose permissions the super admin changed. This is the event that makes permission changes take effect **without logging in again** — rebuild your interface from the new list.

### `queue_updated`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The queue has changed.

A broadcast signal to re-read the queue via `get_queue`. Listeners still get the radio state itself through `sync`.

### `radio_hosts_mode`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Whether the server was built with live host support.

**Payload:** boolean

Sent immediately on connect, without a request.

### `radio_hosts_online`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Whether anyone is on air right now.

**Payload:** boolean

Only sent when `radio_hosts_mode` is enabled.

### `stream_chat_mode_end`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

The conversation ended and the queue resumes.

### `stream_chat_mode_start`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Hosts paused the queue — conversation has begun.

**Payload:**

```js
{ serverTs: … }
```

Duplicates what `sync` shows as `title: "Just chatting"`, but arrives instantly rather than within two seconds.

### `stream_jingle_end`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

The jingle has finished.

### `stream_jingle_start`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

A jingle between songs has started.

**Payload:**

```js
{ jingleId: '…', serverTs: … }
```

Time to hide track metadata: what is playing is not a song.

### `stream_track_start`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

A new track started in the shared stream.

**Payload:**

```js
{ trackId: '…', duration: 214.5, serverTs: 1754899200000 }
```

`serverTs` is the start moment on the server's clock. Combined with your own latency measurement via `stream_ping` this gives an accurate position within the track.

### `suggest_cooldown_update`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

Seconds left before another song can be requested.

**Payload:** number — seconds, 0 when a request is allowed

Sent to every connection sharing the same `uid`, so multiple tabs show the same countdown.

### `suggestion_result`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

The admin's decision on your song request.

**Payload:**

```js
{ accepted: true, auto: false, song: { title, artist, … } }
```

`auto: true` means the request expired on a timer rather than being rejected by hand. Sent only to the socket that made the request.

### `suggestions_update`

<Badge type="info" text="admin" />

The current list of listener song requests.

**Payload:**

```js
[{ uid: '…', song: { id, title, artist }, addedAt: 1754899200000 }]
```

Sent only to admins holding `queue_manage` — on connect, on every change to the list, and when the radio switches to day mode and all requests are cleared.

### `sync`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

The complete radio state. The core event of the protocol.

**Payload:**

```js
{
  track: 'day/artist - title.mp3',  // null while the mode is switching
  title: 'Title', artist: 'Artist', album: 'Album', year: 2020,
  duration: 214.5,
  seek: 87.2,                       // position as of serverTimeMs
  isPlaying: true,
  playlist: [ /* up to 10 upcoming tracks */ ],
  currentIndex: 3, totalTracks: 42,
  mode: 'day',                      // 'day' | 'night'
  pendingModeSwitch: null,
  skipCooldownSecsLeft: 0,
  uiSettings: { /* branding */ },
  serverTimeMs: 1754899200000,
  dayStartHour: 6, nightStartHour: 0,
}
```

Broadcast to everyone every 2 seconds, and once immediately on connect. While the server switches modes a shortened form arrives with `isPreparing: true` and `track: null`. When hosts pause the queue, `title` becomes `"Just chatting"` and `artist` goes empty.

### `usersUpdate`

<Badge type="info" text="listener" />

The list of active listeners, for the header roster.

**Payload:**

```js
[{ name: 'Name', img: 'file.png', color: '#a3f01c' }]
```

Listeners are anonymous: the server assigns each connection a random name from an "oligarchs" set and a random colour. The name arrives already localized.
